liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Truckin' into The Other One has heavy jams and meltdowns; reviewer thinks Bobby skips the first verse; Reviewer calls The Other One epic [8][9]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Reviewer says Pigpen played great organ on Stella Blue at his last show, 6/17/72 [12]
- **Mississippi Half Step** (1 review): Reviewer says this show was the first time Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleloo was played [6]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): About sixteen minutes of jamming precede a short, soothing He's Gone, which returns into The Other One [8]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): Jams between Dickey Betts and Jerry on the Not Fade Away, Goin' Down the Road and Bo Diddley run are praised [3]

## Setlist highlights

- **Hey Bo Diddley**: rare: 5 archived performances [15]
- Earliest performances in the archive: Mississippi Half Step [15]

## The recordings

- **gd72-07-16.sbd-aud.cotsman.11258.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 28 songs; 197 min; rated 4.03/5 by 29 [1]. Said about its sound: Quality is marginal: much of it is a barely passable audience tape, and the board section is somewhat hissy; Attendee says the sound at the venue was much better than this recording; Reviewer hears huge, massive bass; the audience portion is among the worst recordings they know, but set two is big [1][4][5][8][9][13][14]
- **gd1972-07-16.170180.aud.seaweed1010.flac2448**: audience recording; 24 songs; 174 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [2]. Said about its sound: Uploader says the sound is degraded and sometimes hissy [2]

## Around the show

- Dickey Betts, Berry Oakley and Jai Johanny Johanson sat in on starred tracks, with Phil absent from them [3]
- Attendee recalls an open-air track stadium, police in Dead shirts walking the circle and waving to fans, and bright sunshine [5]
- Not Fade Away, Goin' Down the Road and Bo Diddley are starred as the guest-assisted tracks [1]
- Guests Dickey Betts and Berry Oakley joined on Not Fade Away, Goin' Down the Road and Bo Diddley [2]
- Reviewer says this show has been undercirculated until now and is worth getting for the fourth disc [3]
- Few versions of Bo Diddley are available, so the jam with the Allmans is rare [4]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-07-16.sbd-aud.cotsman.11258.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard and Audience composite [1]. Also: Transfer credited via Glenn Gillis and Paul B; an info file has details [1]
- **gd1972-07-16.170180.aud.seaweed1010.flac2448**: taped by liberated from ebay by Seaweed1010; source: Lo-Fi Mono AUD (unknown gear) > unknown gen cassette (c.1990) [2]. Also: This audience recording shares the same root source as the audience tracks of the ID-11258 version [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Dillon Stadium - July 31, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/july-31-1974) [16]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Dillon Stadium - July 31, 1974](https://www.dead.net/show/july-31-1974) [17]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Dillon Stadium - July 16, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/july-16-1972) [18]
